passages.text: So when we could bear it no longer, we were willing to be left on our own in Athens.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions cared deeply for the Thessalonian believers.
They could not endure being apart from them any longer.
They chose to remain alone in Athens.
They made this decision willingly.
passages.original: Διὸ μηκέτι στέγοντες εὐδοκήσαμεν καταλειφθῆναι ἐν Ἀθήναις μόνοι

passages.text: We sent Timothy, our brother and fellow worker for God in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen and encourage you in your faith, so that none of you would be shaken by these trials. For you know that we are destined for this.
passages.sermon:
We sent Timothy to you.
Timothy is our brother.
Timothy works with God in the gospel of Christ.
We sent Timothy to make you strong.
We sent Timothy to encourage you in your faith.
We want none of you to be shaken by these troubles.
You know that we are meant to face these trials.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπέμψαμεν Τιμόθεον τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν καὶ συνεργὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τὸ στηρίξαι ὑμᾶς καὶ παρακαλέσαι ὑπὲρ τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν τὸ μηδένα σαίνεσθαι ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν ταύταις αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἴδατε ὅτι εἰς τοῦτο κείμεθα

passages.text: Indeed, when we were with you, we kept warning you that we would suffer persecution; and as you know, it has come to pass.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul and his companions visited the Thessalonian believers.
Paul and his companions spoke to the Thessalonians.
Paul and his companions warned the Thessalonians.
Paul and his companions said, "We will suffer persecution."
This warning was clear.
Persecution happened, just as Paul and his companions said.
The Thessalonians know this is true.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ὅτε πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἦμεν προελέγομεν ὑμῖν ὅτι μέλλομεν θλίβεσθαι καθὼς καὶ ἐγένετο καὶ οἴδατε

passages.text: For this reason, when I could bear it no longer, I sent to find out about your faith, for fear that the tempter had somehow tempted you and caused our labor to be in vain.
passages.sermon:
I could not bear the uncertainty any longer.
I sent someone to learn about your faith.
I was afraid the tempter might have tempted you.
I feared our work among you might have become useless.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο κἀγὼ μηκέτι στέγων ἔπεμψα εἰς τὸ γνῶναι τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν μή πως ἐπείρασεν ὑμᾶς ὁ πειράζων καὶ εἰς κενὸν γένηται ὁ κόπος ἡμῶν

passages.text: But just now, Timothy has returned from his visit with the good news about your faith, your love, and the fond memories you have preserved, longing to see us just as we long to see you.
passages.sermon:
Timothy has just come back to us from you.
He brought us good news about you.
He told us about your faith.
He told us about your love.
He said you always remember us kindly.
He said you long to see us.
We also long to see you.
passages.original: Ἄρτι δὲ ἐλθόντος Τιμοθέου πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἀφ’ ὑμῶν καὶ εὐαγγελισαμένου ἡμῖν τὴν πίστιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην ὑμῶν καὶ ὅτι ἔχετε μνείαν ἡμῶν ἀγαθὴν πάντοτε ἐπιποθοῦντες ἡμᾶς ἰδεῖν καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: For this reason, brothers, in all our distress and persecution, we have been reassured about you, because of your faith.
passages.sermon:
Brothers, we have suffered much trouble and hardship.
We have faced distress and persecution.
Your faith has encouraged us.
Because of your faith, we feel comforted about you.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο παρεκλήθημεν ἀδελφοί ἐφ’ ὑμῖν ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ ἀνάγκῃ καὶ θλίψει ἡμῶν διὰ τῆς ὑμῶν πίστεως

passages.text: For now we can go on living, as long as you are standing firm in the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Thessalonian believers.
Paul and his companions care deeply about the Thessalonians.
Paul says, “We can continue living now.”
This is true if you stand firm in the Lord.
Your faithfulness gives us strength to go on.
passages.original: ὅτι νῦν ζῶμεν ἐὰν ὑμεῖς στήκετε ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: How can we adequately thank God for you in return for our great joy over you in His presence?
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions speak to the Thessalonian believers.
Paul and his companions feel great joy because of the Thessalonians.
They rejoice before God because of the Thessalonians.
They ask how they can thank God enough for the Thessalonians.
They want to give thanks to God for the joy they have because of the Thessalonians.
passages.original: Τίνα γὰρ εὐχαριστίαν δυνάμεθα τῷ Θεῷ ἀνταποδοῦναι περὶ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ χαρᾷ ᾗ χαίρομεν δι’ ὑμᾶς ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν

passages.text: Night and day we pray most earnestly that we may see you face to face and supply what is lacking from your faith.
passages.sermon:
We pray to God night and day.
We pray with great earnestness.
We pray that we may see you face to face.
We want to supply what is lacking in your faith.
passages.original: νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ δεόμενοι εἰς τὸ ἰδεῖν ὑμῶν τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ καταρτίσαι τὰ ὑστερήματα τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν

passages.text: Now may our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you.
passages.sermon:
God is our Father.
Jesus is our Lord.
We ask God our Father and Jesus our Lord to guide us.
We want God and Jesus to lead us to you.
passages.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ ἡμῶν καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς κατευθύναι τὴν ὁδὸν ἡμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: And may the Lord cause you to increase and overflow with love for one another and for everyone else, just as our love for you overflows, so that He may establish your hearts in blamelessness and holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints. Amen.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is Jesus Christ.
The Lord can make you grow in love.
The Lord can make your love overflow.
You should love one another.
You should love everyone else.
We also love you in this way.
We want your love to be strong and full.
The Lord can make your hearts strong.
He can make your hearts blameless.
He can make your hearts holy.
God is our God and Father.
You will stand before God and our Father.
This will happen when our Lord Jesus comes.
Jesus will come with all His holy people.
Amen.
passages.original: ὑμᾶς δὲ ὁ Κύριος πλεονάσαι καὶ περισσεύσαι τῇ ἀγάπῃ εἰς ἀλλήλους καὶ εἰς πάντας καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς εἰς τὸ στηρίξαι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας ἀμέμπτους ἐν ἁγιωσύνῃ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ μετὰ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων αὐτοῦ ἀμήν
